data.title: Bajaj Housing Finance Earnings Call Shows Robust Growth
data.description:
Bajaj Housing Finance Ltd. ((IN:BAJAJHFL)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Bajaj Housing Finance’s latest earnings call struck a broadly upbeat tone, as management showcased strong growth in assets under management, solid profitability and improving operating efficiency. While they flagged emerging headwinds from rising interest rates, potential pricing pressure and higher operating costs, the positives on growth and asset quality clearly dominated the discussion.

Landmark AUM Milestone and Growth Momentum

AUM crossed INR 1.5 lakh crore for the first time, reaching INR 1.58 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026, underscoring the company’s scale in housing finance. Year-over-year AUM growth held at a robust 25%, with quarterly AUM addition rising to about INR 8,580 crore versus INR 6,329 crore in the same quarter last year.

Broad-Based Disbursement Strength

Disbursements in Q2 FY 2027 climbed 25% year-over-year from INR 15,900 crore to INR 19,900 crore, highlighting sustained demand in the core lending franchise. Home Loan disbursements grew 24% year-over-year, reinforcing housing finance as the central engine of the book.

Profitability Advances Despite Margin Pressure

Quarterly profitability improved meaningfully, with Q2 profit before tax rising 18% year-over-year to INR 980 crore from INR 643 crore. Annualized return on assets was 2.2%, while return on equity inched up to 12.7% from 12.2%, signaling better earnings leverage on the growing balance sheet.

Strong First-Half Financial Delivery

For H1 FY 2027, net total income increased 16% to INR 2,429 crore, while PBT and PAT both rose 20% to INR 1,908 crore and INR 1,472 crore. The company sustained healthy returns, posting a 2.2% ROA and 12.6% ROE for the half-year period.

Operating Efficiency Continues to Improve

Operating efficiency trended in the right direction, with opex-to-NTI improving to 19.1% in Q2 FY 2027 from 19.7% a year earlier. For the first half, the ratio fell from 20.4% to 19.3%, underscoring disciplined cost management even as the company invests in new businesses.

Asset Quality Remains Best-in-Class

Overall asset quality stayed very strong, with gross NPA steady at 29 basis points and net NPA at 12 basis points sequentially. Stage 1 assets improved marginally to 99.40%, Stage 2 assets eased to 31 basis points, and Stage 3 provisioning coverage stood high at 59.8%, giving comfort on future credit losses.

Credit Costs Moderate Further

Credit costs continued to trend lower, with Q2 FY 2027 credit cost at 10 basis points versus 16 basis points in the prior-year quarter. For H1 FY 2027, credit cost was only 8 basis points, reflecting benign delinquencies and strong collection performance.

Diversified Product Growth Across Segments

Growth was broad-based, as Home Loan AUM growth improved to 22% from 20% in the prior quarter, indicating acceleration in the flagship product. Lease rental discounting grew 39% year-over-year, loan against property 26%, and Developer Finance 13%, keeping the AUM mix diversified with Home Loans at 53.9% of the book.

Sambhav Housing Reaches Key Scale Milestones

The Sambhav Housing business crossed a monthly disbursal run rate of INR 500 crore in the quarter and contributed 16% of overall Home Loan originations. With an average ticket size of INR 28 lakh, the segment is increasingly prime, as customers with bureau scores above 750 rose to 65% and salaried borrowers formed 66% of the base.

Sambhav Expansion Strategy Gains Traction

Management said Sambhav is progressing well across B2C, B2B and B2C sourcing channels, underscoring a multi-pronged approach to scale. The company aims to reach or exceed a INR 600 crore monthly disbursal run rate by year-end and gradually lift Sambhav to around 20% of the Home Loan mix next year and 30% over the next three to four years.

Lower Cost of Funds and Better Gross Spread

Cost of funds declined 17 basis points sequentially from 7.2% in Q1 to about 7% in Q2, mainly driven by converting fixed-rate liabilities into floating-rate instruments. Gross spread improved 7 basis points to 1.8%, helping offset a 10-basis-point reduction in portfolio yield and supporting overall profitability.

Diversified Borrowing Profile Supports Stability

The borrowing mix remained diversified, with money market instruments at 56%, bank lines at 35% and NHB funding at 9%. Within this, NCDs rose to 50.8%, up 430 basis points sequentially, partially replacing bank borrowing, commercial paper and NHB, and strengthening market-based funding.

Healthy Capital and Regulatory Buffers

Capital adequacy stood at a comfortable 21.24%, providing room to support growth without immediate capital needs. The principal business criterion was 60.49% and individual Home Loan criterion 50.6%, both above regulatory thresholds, confirming compliance with key sector norms.

Expanded Branch Network Underpins Growth

The operating network expanded to 223 branches across 182 locations, enhancing physical reach into newer geographies. This footprint supports both prime and near-prime expansion and underlies the strong disbursement and AUM growth trends reported.

Higher Fee Income from Cross-Sell

Fee and commission income rose, helped by higher insurance income and increased foreclosure fees. Management linked the insurance uptick to stronger Sambhav disbursements and better attachment rates, confirming that cross-sell remains an important earnings lever.

Continued Investment in Near-Prime and New Markets

Management emphasized sustained investment in Sambhav and the non-top-six market structure to build long-term franchises. The company plans to continue investing heavily in near-prime segments, top-six-plus markets this year, and affordable housing in the next year, even at the cost of higher near-term expenses.

Floating-Rate Balance Sheet Shapes Rate Sensitivity

Around 88% of assets and liabilities are on floating rates, creating a largely matched interest-rate profile. Management expects about 80% to 82% of future repo hikes to flow through to cost of funds, with similar pass-through to portfolio yields, limiting structural margin risk but heightening short-term volatility.

Developer Finance Growth Commitment

Although the Developer Finance portfolio declined sequentially due to higher project-led repayments and slower disbursements, management stressed this was not a strategic pullback. Sanctions rose sharply in the first half, and the company targets Developer Finance growth of around 15% to 17% of the portfolio over time.

Assignment Strategy Within Defined Corridor

The company assigned about INR 1,428 crore of loans in the quarter versus INR 2,600 crore in the previous quarter, indicating tactical moderation. Management reiterated that assignments will generally stay within an 11% to 13% corridor of the book, guided by principal business criteria and asset-liability management considerations.

Sequential NIM and Yield Moderation

Net interest margin moderated by 10 basis points sequentially to 3.7%, reflecting lower portfolio yields and changing funding dynamics. Portfolio yield dipped from 8.9% in Q1 to 8.8% in Q2, a modest decline that management is watching amid a shifting rate environment.

Developer Finance Portfolio Movement

The Developer Finance portfolio’s sequential decline was driven by higher repayments and slower disbursements rather than asset-quality weakness. Management noted that, despite the quarter-on-quarter drop, the business still grew 13% year-over-year, supporting its medium-term growth intentions.

Marginal Uptick in Home Loan GNPA

Home Loan GNPA increased slightly to 36 basis points from 34 basis points in the previous quarter, while Home Loan NNPA rose by 1 basis point to 16 basis points. Management described this as a modest deterioration within an otherwise strong Home Loan asset-quality profile.

Isolated LRD Account Migration to NPA

LRD GNPA came in at 2 basis points following the movement of a single retail LRD account from Stage 2 to Stage 3. Excluding this one account, management said the LRD portfolio remains strong, indicating no broad-based stress in the segment.

Potential Impact from Insurance Commission Rules

Management cautioned that final insurance commission guidelines, if similar to the draft, could impact income from cross-sell. With roughly 10% to 11% of PBT coming from cross-sell and only 4% to 5% likely offset, the company anticipates a possible 6% to 7% hit to PBT and sees opex-to-NTI potentially flat next year under that scenario.

Rising Salary Expenses Reflect Growth Investments

Salary expenses increased 19% year-over-year in the quarter, driven by higher headcount, senior leadership hires and continued investment in Sambhav and other businesses. Management expects salary costs to keep rising year-over-year for the next four quarters before stabilizing, highlighting a deliberate build-out phase.

Prime-Market Pricing and Attrition Risk

Management flagged that higher repo rates could lift cost of funds, with uncertainty around whether banks will raise new acquisition pricing accordingly. If pricing does not keep pace, the company could face higher attrition, particularly in prime housing and some LRD loans, pressuring both growth and margins.

Guidance Held Amid Rate Uncertainty

The company did not revise guidance, noting that the full impact of the recent rate hike on acquisition pricing and balance transfers is still unclear. It indicated AUM growth could ease from 25% toward 22% to 23% if attrition increases, while margin pressure could add 1 to 2 basis points if acquisition pricing lags funding costs.

Expected Cost of Funds Trend Higher

Management called the roughly 7% September exit cost of funds a starting point for an upward trajectory as rates rise. In a scenario of three 25-basis-point repo hikes, it estimated that around 60 to 61 basis points could flow through to cost of funds by the exit period, underscoring the importance of pricing discipline.

Lower Income from De-Recognized Loans

Income from de-recognized loans fell to about INR 40 crore in the quarter from roughly INR 68 crore previously, mainly due to lower assignment volume. Assignments declined to around INR 1,428 crore versus INR 2,600 crore, trimming this ancillary income stream.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Strategic Priorities

Management reaffirmed yearly AUM growth guidance of 21% to 23% and ROA of 2.1% to 2.3%, while flagging around 25 basis points of NIM compression for the year, with a further one or two basis points possible if pricing pressure persists. It expects Developer Finance to grow at 15% to 17% of the portfolio, Sambhav to hit a INR 600 crore monthly disbursal run rate by year-end and reach around 20% of the Home Loan mix next year and 30% over three to four years, while assignments remain at 11% to 13% of the book and opex-to-NTI is reduced by 1% each year.

The earnings call painted a picture of a lender that is scaling rapidly, protecting asset quality and investing for the future, even as it prepares for a tougher rate and regulatory backdrop. For investors, Bajaj Housing Finance’s blend of strong growth, tight credit costs and clear strategic focus on Sambhav and diversified products suggests a resilient franchise, though near-term margins and fee income bear watching as rates and rules evolve.

data.title: BNY Mellon Q3 Earnings Call Signals Strong Momentum
data.description:
The Bank Of New York Mellon Corporation ((BNY)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

BNY Mellon struck an upbeat tone on its latest earnings call, framing the quarter as a powerful proof point for its transformation strategy. Management highlighted double-digit revenue growth, sharply higher earnings and sustained commercial momentum across core franchises. While acknowledging expense pressure, capital ratio drift and market volatility, executives emphasized improving profitability and raised full‑year operating targets.

Strong Third-Quarter Earnings and Profitability

BNY Mellon delivered a standout third quarter, with earnings per share rising 24% year-over-year to $2.34, or $2.37 excluding notable items. Pretax margin widened to 39%, return on tangible common equity hit 29%, and the bank generated roughly 390 basis points of positive operating leverage, signaling that revenue is growing much faster than costs.

Broad-Based Revenue Growth

Revenue momentum was not confined to one business line, underscoring the breadth of demand for BNY Mellon’s services. Firm-wide revenue climbed 12% year-over-year to $5.7 billion, while fee revenue also rose 12%, a notable achievement in a mixed market backdrop and a key driver of the quarter’s profitability gains.

Sustained Commercial Momentum

Sales activity remained robust across geographies, products and client segments, reinforcing the company’s growth narrative. The quarter marked BNY Mellon’s 15th consecutive period of year-over-year sales growth, featuring larger, more comprehensive mandates and marquee relationships with clients such as Revolut and ING that deepen its strategic positioning.

Investment Services and Asset Growth

Investment services was again a core engine, with fees up 15% year-over-year on net new business, higher client activity and stronger markets. Assets under custody or administration reached $63.4 trillion, up 10%, driven by net inflows and new mandates, even as currency headwinds muted some of the reported growth.

Foreign Exchange and Net Interest Income Growth

Trading-linked businesses showed solid traction, with foreign exchange revenue up 19% year-over-year on higher client volumes and product innovation. Net interest income rose 15% to $1.4 billion, helped by reinvesting securities at higher yields and balance sheet growth, although sequential pressure from deposits and margins hinted at a tougher near-term rate backdrop.

Securities Services Expansion

Securities Services posted outsized gains, underscoring BNY Mellon’s scale advantage in core infrastructure. Segment revenue reached $2.8 billion, up 15%, while investment services fees soared 19% and pretax income jumped 24% to $1 billion with a 36% margin, aided by strong ETF, alternatives and debt servicing volumes.

Issuer Services and Depositary Receipts Wins

Issuer Services delivered one of the call’s standout growth stories, benefiting from broad-based corporate trust demand. Investment services fees in the unit surged 43%, while Depositary Receipts revenue grew at a double-digit pace and the bank reported winning roughly two-thirds of capital-raising activity year-to-date, cementing its leadership in this niche.

Market and Wealth Services Growth

Market and Wealth Services showed strong operating leverage, combining growth with high margins. Revenue rose 12% to $2 billion, pretax income increased 17% and pretax margin reached an impressive 51%, supported by a 17% jump in Clearance and Collateral fees, higher collateral balances and rising daily transaction volumes.

Wealth Solutions Net New Assets

Wealth Solutions continued to build scale, even as broader asset management flows were mixed. The business generated $48 billion of net new assets in the quarter, a 7% annualized growth rate, while winning new client logos, renewing multiyear contracts and lifting investment services fees 7%, reinforcing its medium-term growth potential.

Payments, Trade and Lending Momentum

BNY Mellon’s transaction-led franchise showed healthy expansion, reflecting the bank’s role in global cash and trade flows. Payments and Trade investment services fees rose 8% on new wins and higher payment volumes, while average loans grew 19%, largely in short-duration, fully collateralized secured finance that supports client activity without materially stretching risk.

Investment and Wealth Management Profitability

The broader Investment and Wealth Management segment delivered modest top-line growth but improved efficiency. Revenue climbed 4% year-over-year to $857 million, while pretax income rose 11% to $205 million and margin improved to 24%, showing that even with AUM headwinds, the franchise can translate incremental revenue into better profitability.

Platform Operating Model Fully Implemented

Management emphasized that its platform operating model is now fully live across the firm, a key milestone in its transformation journey. Efficiency gains harvested over recent years are being redirected into growth initiatives, with the new structure designed to enhance client value, cross-platform delivery and commercial outcomes rather than simply cutting costs.

Digital Asset and Payments Innovation

The call highlighted BNY Mellon’s push into tokenization and digital payments as a differentiator versus peers. The bank launched global Digital Transfer Agency capabilities, extended fund servicing to on-chain assets and introduced BLIQUID tokens tied to a digital money market fund, alongside partnerships with Baillie Gifford and BlackRock and a Pay-to-Wallet solution for cross-border flows.

Expansion of AI Capabilities

Artificial intelligence featured prominently as a strategic growth vector for the firm. BNY Mellon reported more than 400 AI solutions in production via its Eliza platform, focused on efficiency gains, product improvements and new client offerings, and it has opened the BNY AI Lab with Carnegie Mellon University to deepen research and talent ties.

Capital Returns and Liquidity Position

Shareholder returns remained robust despite modest pressure on capital ratios. The bank returned about $1.4 billion to common shareholders in the quarter, an 85% total payout ratio, and management said it still feels comfortable with its capital and liquidity, noting the Tier 1 leverage ratio remains within its 5.5% to 6% target range.

Uneven and Volatile Operating Environment

Executives repeatedly acknowledged that the macro backdrop remains tricky, even as it remains broadly supportive. Persistent inflation, sharp rate repricing, geopolitical tensions and trade uncertainty have driven volatility in fixed income and rotations in equity markets, shaping client behavior and underlining the need for risk discipline.

Assets Under Management Affected by Outflows and Currency

Despite rising markets, asset management metrics were more muted and highlighted competitive pressures. Assets under management reached $2.2 trillion, up just 2% year-over-year, as higher market values were offset by cumulative net outflows and the drag from a stronger U.S. dollar, with fee growth similarly tempered by mix effects.

Cash Strategy Outflows

Within investment and wealth operations, flows revealed a notable shift away from cash. The unit recorded $6 billion of net inflows in long-term active strategies and $4 billion into index products, but these gains were more than offset by $22 billion of net outflows in cash, reflecting clients reallocating liquidity in response to rate and market moves.

Sequential Net Interest Income and Deposit Declines

While net interest income was strong year-on-year, the sequential trend signaled some pressure from the rate cycle. NII eased 2% quarter-over-quarter to $1.4 billion, average deposit balances fell 1%, and margins compressed, suggesting that competitive pricing and client repositioning are weighing on near-term spread income despite overall growth.

Higher Expenses and Increased Expense Guidance

Cost trends were a key watchpoint for investors, as spending rose faster than many peers. Expenses increased 8% year-over-year to $3.5 billion, with most linked to revenue-related items and higher investment, partially offset by efficiency savings, and the bank lifted its 2026 expense growth outlook by 100 basis points to the mid-point of a 7% to 8% range.

Lower Capital Ratios

Capital ratios edged lower, reflecting the balance between returning cash and maintaining buffers. Tier 1 leverage dipped 24 basis points sequentially to 5.7%, Tier 1 capital fell by $1.1 billion, and the CET1 ratio slipped to 10.9%, impacted by capital returns, accumulated other comprehensive income movements and preferred stock actions.

Foreign Exchange Headwind

Currency movements proved a subtle but real drag on reported metrics, even amid strong client flows. Management noted that the stronger U.S. dollar partly offset growth in assets under custody or administration and in assets under management, a reminder that global scale brings both diversification benefits and FX sensitivity.

Fourth-Quarter Seasonal Cost Pressures

Investors were cautioned to expect a typical seasonal uptick in costs into year-end. Fourth-quarter expenses are set to rise on compensation-related items, vendor payments and other idiosyncratic factors that are individually small but collectively meaningful, though management urged markets not to treat this higher run-rate as the baseline for next year.

AI Governance and Safety Challenges

Alongside its bullish stance on AI, BNY Mellon struck a cautious note on governance and risk. Management warned that adoption can be constrained by alignment and observability challenges, especially with open-weight models that can bypass embedded safeguards, necessitating continued investment in safety protocols and robust controls.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

Looking ahead to 2026, BNY Mellon raised its operating outlook and now targets nearly 500 basis points of positive operating leverage. The bank expects revenue growth excluding notable items to be around the middle of a 12% to 13% range, net interest income up 15%, expenses rising mid-7% to 8%, modest deposit growth, steady securities roll-off and a Tier 1 leverage ratio held within its 5.5% to 6% framework.

BNY Mellon’s latest earnings call painted a picture of a company leaning into growth, technology and client demand while navigating familiar macro and cost headwinds. Double-digit revenue gains, strong margins and an upgraded operating outlook offer a constructive story for shareholders, even as expenses, capital ratios and market volatility remain key metrics to watch in coming quarters.

data.title: Conduent Reaches Class Action Cybersecurity Settlement Agreement

data.title: GBank Financial Names Interim Finance Leadership Team
data.description:
GBank Financial Holdings ( (GBFH) ) has shared an announcement.

On October 12, 2026, GBank Financial Holdings reported that Olivia M.
